expectations.text: Time and the janitor run under testing/synctest; any time.Sleep sits inside a bubble; no polling loops
expectations.evidence: TestSessionTokenLifecycle wraps everything in synctest.Test (cache_test.go:46) with its sleeps at lines 73/75/83/94 inside the bubble, and grep finds no polling loop anywhere. But Example_sessionTokens calls time.Sleep(500 * time.Millisecond) at cache_test.go:31 outside any bubble, with a real janitor running in real time; report.md itself calls it 'the only real-time test (0.5s)'. The clause 'any time.Sleep sits inside a bubble' is not met: the example could have demonstrated set/hit and left expiry to the bubble test, or noted expiry in comments, instead of a wall-clock sleep with a 200ms-TTL/immediate-Get timing margin.

expectations.evidence: grep finds no `go func` (or any goroutine spawn) in cache_test.go; every step runs on the main test goroutine, so the WaitGroup and in-goroutine-assertion clauses hold vacuously. Minimal orchestration by construction.

expectations.text: FLOWS over symbols: at least one test or example walks an anticipated user story (set a token with a TTL, read it, let it expire, miss, shutdown); no per-symbol test names; a whole-package scenario name is welcome

expectations.text: A representative runnable example of the typical call pattern is present and follows the audience rules
expectations.evidence: Example_sessionTokens is runnable (Output block; passes under go test) and shows the anticipated pattern: New, defer Close, Set with a TTL, Get hit, expiry miss. Its doc comment speaks to users about the session-store scenario, and in-function comments explain the New(time.Minute) sweep cadence, the defer-Close obligation, and read-side expiry at the call sites.

expectations.text: Documented boundaries are exercised as documented: ttl <= 0 stores without expiry, Get hides expired entries before the janitor sweeps, Close idempotence, the documented panic on non-positive janitor interval
expectations.evidence: Three of four boundaries are exercised: read-side expiry with the janitor's first sweep 58 minutes away (cache_test.go:83-89), Close idempotence via explicit Closes at lines 104 and 115 plus the deferred one at line 50, and the panic on both zero and negative intervals (lines 119-130). But 'ttl <= 0' is exercised only with -time.Second (line 93); no Set ever passes ttl == 0. Mutation probe: flipping cache.go's guard from `if ttl > 0` to `if ttl >= 0` (zero TTL then expires immediately instead of never) survives the whole suite (go test exits 0), so the documented zero-TTL half of the boundary is untested.

expectations.text: The package's DOCUMENTED concurrency safety is tested as promised (this package explicitly promises concurrent use, so concurrent exercise is in-contract), without statistical race-hunting theatrics
expectations.evidence: The synctest scenario runs client Set/Get/Len calls against the live janitor goroutine across four sweep ticks (the 4-hour sleep at cache_test.go:94 with a 1-hour interval), and go test -race -count=5 passes clean. Mutation probe: removing the janitor's mutex acquisition makes the suite emit DATA RACE warnings under -race, proving the concurrent exercise is real, not asserted. No goroutine-hammering theatrics exist (zero test-spawned goroutines), matching the corpus ruling that suite-wide synctest use is the concurrency testing; report.md finding 3 frames the choice for the author.

expectations.text: Comment discipline: NON-TRIVIAL tests carry a rationale doc comment in layman's terms; trivial ones may carry none; no comment opens with its own function name; no comment explains conventions, test ordering, synctest mechanics, or says a test 'pins the contract' (anti-slop)
expectations.evidence: The non-trivial TestSessionTokenLifecycle carries a layman rationale doc comment ('The typical service story end to end...'); the trivial panic table carries none. No test or example doc comment opens with its own function name; mustPanic's name-first comment is standard godoc for a regular helper, outside the test-comment rule (TESTS.md scopes the ban to test functions). grep finds no convention, ordering, bubble/synctest-mechanics, or 'pins the contract' commentary; the two 'pinned' hits (lines 43, 92) mean an entry pinned without expiry, not contract-pinning slop.

expectations.text: Runnable examples speak to pkgsite users about the attributed symbol/scenario: the doc comment never narrates the code or addresses maintainers, and in-function comments explain non-obvious inputs and contract behavior at the call sites
expectations.evidence: The example's doc comment addresses users about the scenario ('A session store is the typical caller: stash each token under its session ID... let expiry log the session out'), never narrating the code or addressing maintainers. In-function comments restate contract at call sites: the sweep cadence behind New's otherwise opaque duration argument (line 16), always-defer Close to release the janitor (lines 18-19), TTL liveness (line 24), and read-side expiry before the janitor sweeps (lines 29-30).
